column3:
AI got about 80% cheaper this week. It did not get any smarter.

OpenAI cut Luna API pricing 80%, to $0.20 per million input tokens. The model behind that price did not change at all. Only the code that serves it did.

Three labs moved in the same week. Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5 at the same $5 per million input tokens it already charged, and it matches or beats Fable 5 on most benchmarks. Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash does the same work with 17% fewer tokens, which is a discount that shows up as smaller usage instead of a smaller sticker price.

Here is why that combination is unusual. Cheaper used to mean weaker. You waited for a new model to get a better price. This week the price moved on its own.

What it means for you: the feature you shelved because you could not run it on every customer is worth pricing again this week, before you redesign it.

One honest catch. An 80% list cut is not an 80% invoice. How many tokens you send, how much context you stuff in, and how often you retry still decide what you actually pay.

What did you park because it cost too much? Drop it in the comments.
